speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the resignation rate among Singaporean employees in the last two years as compared to before; (b) whether Singapore is seeing a wave of resignations like in other countries; (c) with the rise of remote work, whether the resignation trend will become more prevalent as employees have more choices and less workplace camaraderie to retain them; and (d) which industries are struggling with employee retention and how is the Government helping them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is yet another example of where the Singapore labour market has responded to COVID-19 differently from other economies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have similarly seen that the employment rates for women and senior workers have not dropped but have held steady or continued to rise.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Analysts, observers and commentators interested in labour market issues may want to consider that there are factors that do not allow for a like-for-like comparison with the situation in many other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, the IHRP's COVID-19 Taskforce curated several resources to help employers and the HR community navigate the changes and challenges posed by the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, the People Strategy HR toolkit offers a series of guides on talent attraction, development and retention.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Companies and HR professionals are strongly encouraged to take reference from the recommended approaches and best practices to refresh their talent management strategies and reduce staff turnover.
